content:
Some memory chips used in Apple devices could be manufactured in the US for the first time if plans involving one of the company's suppliers go ahead.

The latest reports say Apple memory supplier SK Hynix is in talks with Intel about potentially using Intel's planned chip factory in Ohio...

According to Reuters, details remain unclear, but the Korean company produces RAM and flash memory chips for Apple devices.

Some processors used in Apple devices are already manufactured domestically in the US, but due to restrictions on using TSMC's most advanced processes overseas, this currently only applies to older models. However, DRAM or NAND flash memory chips are not subject to this restriction, as Apple uses industry-standard versions.

However, reports indicate the plans could face opposition from the South Korean government, as South Korea, like Taiwan, may be concerned about the export of chip manufacturing technology, even when involving less advanced processes.

SK Hynix says nothing has been finalised. Intel declined to comment on the report but confirmed it will continue to push ahead with plans for the Ohio facility.
